differences.what: massing: a long, low, one-storey house with its ridge along the river front, the front about two and a half times the gable end
differences.how: T-2509: log_dwelling on a 14.6 x 5.5 m plan with a 2.4 m wall. The camera is fitted to the front's four corners, so their landing is not a test; the test is the ridge, whose right end the record's 30 degree roof puts at (380.4, 163.2) against the plate's (379.3, 167.1)

differences.what: the river front's openings: three doors and six small windows in the order window, door, window, window, door, window, window, door, window; the build has the archetype's one door between two windows
differences.how: log_dwelling builds its front from core_front_rects, one door and two windows a storey, and states no other set-out. Giving it one is an archetype change that re-hashes every log dwelling's mesh: T-2511

differences.what: the stack: the plate stands it outside the LEFT (upstream) gable as seen from the river; the build stands it against the right (downstream) gable
differences.how: log_dwelling always puts a single stack at the low end of the ridge's axis (_chimneys, at_min=True), and the record cannot choose the end: T-2511

differences.what: a lower gabled lean-to beyond the stack at the left end, drawn gable-on to the viewer
differences.how: log_dwelling's frame_addition is a FRAME addition and builds clapboard, not a log or plank lean-to, and stands its stack differently: T-2511. The lean-to's own perspective disagrees with the main roof's, so its size is read only roughly

differences.what: the walls: the plate draws them smooth and pale with no courses and no notched corners, as whitewash or as a wash drawing's convention; the build shows round logs with saddle-notched corners
differences.how: Currey's text calls it a log cabin (lines 1456-1457) and the record grades construction 'log' attested on that; whether the plate's pale walls are whitewash or the illustrator's shorthand cannot be settled from a monochrome wash drawing, so it is left open for T-2511 to rule on rather than built either way

differences.what: the roof's tone: the plate draws the roof much darker than the walls; the build's shingles are pale
differences.how: Tone, not colour: a monochrome print can still say the roof was darker than the walls. Weathered shakes or bark would read so; the build's roof finish is the archetype's. T-2511

differences.what: the back wall and the right (downstream) gable
differences.how: The plate sees the front and the left end only

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
note: Reviewed by T-2509 against the side-by-side. The plate is a retrospective wash drawing (tier 5) by an unnamed illustrator, about a century after the farm, and may as well show the later trading house on the same premises; it is still the one picture of the place, and the image gate builds toward it. The massing and the roof's height agree; the opening set-out, the stack's end, the lean-to, the walls' finish and the roof's tone do not, and each needs the log_dwelling archetype to state what it builds today by rule. That change re-hashes all 72 log dwellings, which is T-2511's run, not this one.
